To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Arabidopsis Ser-Arg-Arg-rich protein SHW1 promotes the COP1-mediated degradation and the consequent down-regulation of HY5, and this is required for the normal growth of Arabidopsis seedlings in the darkness.
SHW1 interacts with COP1 and negatively regulates the stability of HY5 protein in darkness.

the Arabidopsis Ser/Arg-rich protein SHW1 interacts with COP1 and negatively regulates COP1-mediated ubiquitylation and degradation of HY5, which results in promotion of photomorphogenic seedling development.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular and genetic interactions among SHW1, HY5, and COP1 in Arabidopsis photomorphogenesis and seedling development.
the regulation of photomorphogenic development by COP1 and HY 5 in Arabidopis.
the functional interaction of SHW1 and COP1 in Arabidopsis photomorphogenesis and seedling development.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

SHW1 is a novel negative regulator of phototropism that acts as a scaffold protein to promote COP1-mediated HY5 degradation in the darkness, and thus plays a role in regulating photomorphogenic seedling growth.
SHW1 interacts physically and genetically with HY5 and COP1 to regulate seedling photomorphogenesis and root gravitropism.
the SHW1 protein physically interacts with the COP1 and HY 5 proteins, and SHW1 functions in the same pathway as COP1 and HY  5.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
SHW1 functions in the COP1-HY5 module in a positive manner to promote photomorphogenesis and negatively regulates COP1-HY1 module in a negative manner for the promotion of skotomorphogenesis.
SHW1 functions as a positive regulator of COP1-mediated degradation and a negative regulator of HY5-mediated photomorphogenesis during seedling development.
SHW1 interacts with both COP and HY5, and SHW1 promotes HY5 degradation in the darkness through enhancing COP1-mediated ubiquitylation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
SHW1 interacts with HY5 and COP1 and acts as a positive regulator of COP1-HY5 interaction in promoting COP1-mediated degradation.
a novel negative regulator, SHW1, of light signaling is able to promote COP1-mediated degradation and antagonize the function of HY5, which is a key transcription factor for light signaling.
the Ser-Arg-Arg rich protein, SHW1, interacts with both HY5 and COP1, and it promotes the degradation of HY5 by COP1 in the darkness.
